hypothesis: Constitutional BRCA1 promoter methylation (12.4%–33.9% of TNBC depending on cohort age-selection; WHI 12.4%, Institut Curie 20.6%, early-onset ≤30yr 33.9%) produces HRD genomic scars (LOH, TAI, LST) and pre-treatment RAD51 foci failure functionally equivalent to germline BRCA1 mutation, and this population — currently excluded from PARPi eligibility criteria — derives olaparib benefit specifically in the TREATMENT-NAIVE setting before epigenetic reversion of BRCA1 silencing can occur. Unlike stable germline BRCA1 mutations, constitutional methylation-driven HRD is reversible: neoadjuvant chemotherapy exposure is sufficient to induce BRCA1 re-expression and RAD51 restoration, conferring acquired olaparib resistance. PARPi eligibility expansion for constitutional methylation-positive TNBC is therefore contingent on first-line (chemotherapy-naive) treatment context.
additional_claim: Constitutional BRCA1 methylation-positive TNBC undergoes BRCA1 re-expression via RAD51 restoration after chemotherapy exposure, conferring PARPi resistance — suggesting a race-to-treatment window analogous to platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer: early-line PARPi maximizes benefit before re-expression occurs
testable_experiment: Two-arm prospective-translational pilot study in TNBC patients with confirmed constitutional BRCA1 methylation (allele-specific blood-based pyrosequencing): Arm A (treatment-naive) — first-line olaparib monotherapy with pre-treatment biopsy RAD51 foci assay (IF, FFPE-compatible); Arm B (post-neoadjuvant) — olaparib after standard NACT with paired baseline/post-NACT biopsies for BRCA1 mRNA (RT-qPCR), BRCA1 protein (IHC), and RAD51 foci quantification. Primary endpoint: olaparib IC50 shift between Arm A and Arm B. Secondary: RAD51 positivity rate (>10% nuclei = HR-restored threshold) as predictor of olaparib non-response. Companion: BRCA1 methylation allele fraction in blood pre/post NACT to test epigenetic reversion at germline level. This directly tests the treatment-naive window hypothesis and establishes RAD51 restoration as the actionable biomarker gating re-treatment eligibility.
revised_novelty_claim: No published PARPi trial has (1) enrolled constitutional BRCA1 methylation-positive TNBC as a distinct eligibility stratum, nor (2) tested the treatment-naive vs pre-treated distinction as a predictor of PARPi benefit in this population. The HR reversibility finding (Frontiers Oncol 2023) is established for methylated TNBC generically; its specific application to CONSTITUTIONAL (blood-confirmed, not tumor-somatic) methylation carriers as a therapeutic scoping criterion is a novel clinical inference. The race-to-treatment window framing — analogous to platinum-sensitive ovarian relapse — is not present in any published PARPi-TNBC trial design.
refinement_changes_from_v1: Prevalence updated from single-point 20.6% to range 12.4%–33.9% across four independent cohorts (WHI JAMA Oncol 2022, Institut Curie PMID 41654537, Clinical Epigenetics 2025, Genome Medicine 2023)
Hypothesis now explicitly scoped to treatment-naive TNBC — removes applicability to post-NACT setting
Added epigenetic reversibility mechanism: BRCA1 re-expression via RAD51 foci restoration post-chemotherapy (Frontiers Oncol 2023 evidence)
Added race-to-treatment window framing as the clinical implication of reversibility
Key targets expanded to include RAD51_foci_pre_treatment and BRCA1_re_expression_post_chemo as mechanistic endpoints
Testable experiment redesigned to directly compare treatment-naive vs post-NACT arms rather than retrospective biobank re-analysis only

evidence_basis.role: Independent prevalence replication — WHI US population 12.4%
Founding prevalence study — 20.6% constitutional methylation in TNBC, HRD scar association
Age-enriched prevalence upper bound — 33.9% in early-onset TNBC
CRITICAL reversibility evidence: RAD51 foci restored in methylated TNBC post-NACT; HR is reversible unlike germline mutation
HRD scar equivalence (LOH/TAI/LST) methylated vs mutated BRCA1 TNBC confirmed
RAD51 foci assay feasibility in TNBC FFPE tissue confirmed

composite_delta_rationale: Plausibility slightly elevated (0.82 → 0.84) because reversibility mechanism strengthens mechanistic coherence of the scoped hypothesis. Actionability slightly reduced (0.88 → 0.85) because treatment-naive arm requires prospective design rather than retrospective biobank re-analysis. Evidential quality improves from single-source to multi-cohort but olaparib response in treatment-naive constitutional methylation carriers is still unpublished data. Net composite: 0.810 as per reflexion-tnbc-001 revised estimate.
scope_boundary: This hypothesis applies ONLY to treatment-naive (chemotherapy-unexposed) TNBC at time of PARPi administration. For post-NACT patients with constitutional BRCA1 methylation, olaparib benefit is NOT predicted — RAD51 restoration must be explicitly tested by functional assay before re-enrollment.
therapeutic_analogy: Platinum-sensitive ovarian cancer relapse window: benefit is time/exposure-bounded, not genotype-permanent. Methylation-positive TNBC should be treated as an 'epigenetically sensitive' window analogous to platinum-free interval.
next_steps: Prioritize: experiment-design-tnbc-001v2 — SUM149PT vs HCC1937 cisplatin/olaparib reversibility assay (see companion experiment file)
Biobank query: OlympiAD/EMBRACA — stratify by treatment-naive vs post-NACT at time of PARPi enrollment for constitutional methylation carriers
Clinical trial design: first-in-class arm for treatment-naive constitutional methylation TNBC in ongoing PARPi maintenance trials
